sentences.text: Chinshakiangosaurus is a genus of basal sauropod dinosaur.
The single known individual measured between 12 and 13 meters in total body length.
Its lower jaw was curved when viewed from above, creating a wide, U-shaped snout common among sauropods.
Each side of the mandible held nineteen teeth, a count higher than any other known sauropod but lower than the prosauropod Plateosaurus.
A distinct diagonal ridge on the jawbone suggests the animal had fleshy cheeks, a trait previously seen only in prosauropods.
The fossil record includes parts of the skull, several vertebrae, shoulder blades, hip bones, and leg bones.
Zhao Xijin and his team discovered the remains in 1970 within Yongren County in central Yunnan.
The bones were extracted from the Fengjiahe Formation, which consists of mudstone, siltstone, and sandstone laid down in river and lake settings.
Associated invertebrate fossils point to an Upper Jurassic age, although a precise dating was not possible.
C. H. Ye assigned the name Chinshakiangosaurus chunghoensis in 1975, honoring the Yangtze River and the nearby village of Zhonghe.
This name was considered invalid as a nomen nudum until Dong Zhiming provided a formal description in 1992.
The holotype specimen, cataloged as IVPP V14474, contains a left dentary, one neck vertebra, several back and tail vertebrae, both shoulder blades, some pelvic bones, and hind limb elements.
Scientists propose that the wide snout indicates a bulk-feeding lifestyle adapted for consuming large quantities of vegetation, contrasting with selective feeders that have tapered snouts.
A bony plate lining the tooth row likely stopped the teeth from shifting while the animal stripped plants.
Fleshy cheeks would have kept food inside the mouth and might suggest some chewing or processing occurred before swallowing.
Dong Zhiming originally placed Chinshakiangosaurus within the prosauropod group Melanorosauridae.
Modern research classifies the genus as a very basal sauropod.
The parent group for this dinosaur is Sauropoda.
Chinshakiangosaurus belongs to the broader class Saurischia.
The exact evolutionary relationships of Chinshakiangosaurus remain uncertain.
Debate continues over whether the genus is a valid taxon, with some earlier works labeling it a nomen dubium.
Chinshakiangosaurus lived during the Early Jurassic period.
It inhabited Asia approximately 185 million years ago during the Toarcian stage of the Early Jurassic.
Other data suggest the animal lived during the Hettangian stage, spanning from 201.4 to 199.5 million years ago.
